title: Ambiguity-Robust Decision and Minimax Regret Evaluation
purpose: Compare point-probability decisions, worst-case expected-loss decisions and minimax-regret decisions under explicit total-variation ambiguity sets for Bernoulli severe-loss events.
scope_limits: All forecasts, probability intervals, event observations, cost profiles, ambiguity radii and review fallbacks are fictional public-development data.
NRES-012 reuses the 128 public synthetic NRES-011 cases and is a linked benchmark increment, not independent confirmation.
The probability interval is a declared total-variation ambiguity set around a Bernoulli event probability; it is not a conformal confidence interval or a statistically calibrated prediction interval.
For Bernoulli distributions, total variation distance equals the absolute difference in event probabilities, so the ambiguity set is a closed interval.
All costs are normalized fictional planning-loss units, not currency, budgets or operational instructions.
No policy is legally authorized, operationally executable or causal-effect validated.
For missing/conflicting inputs, the model must abstain and the separately supplied human-review fallback is used; no point or interval forecast is emitted.
The benchmark compares deterministic decision rules on declared uncertainty sets; it does not train a decision-focused model or prove optimality under arbitrary shifts.

source_fixture.source_description: Every source_case_id maps one-to-one to the pinned NRES-011 synthetic forecast/observation fixture. Candidate point probabilities, evaluator truth, scenario strata and review fallbacks are copied exactly.

sampling_design.design_note: 24 routine and 8 tail-enriched cases per regime; estimates target the declared 97%/3% stratum mixture only if cases are representative within their respective strata.

calibration_reference.description: Fictional historical training cohort used only to construct a fixed climatology comparison. It is not a real event base rate.

protocol.nominal_policy: prepare if point probability >= profile cost/loss threshold; otherwise no_action
protocol.worst_case_expected_loss_policy: choose the action with the lower maximum expected loss over q in [lower,upper]; exact ties choose no_action
protocol.minimax_regret_policy: choose the action with the lower maximum regret over q in [lower,upper]; exact ties choose no_action
protocol.worst_case_regret: no_action regret=max(0, upper*(L0-L1)-C); prepare regret=max(0, C-lower*(L0-L1))
protocol.review_policy: all abstentions use the evaluator-owned review_fallback_action plus the profile deferral cost
protocol.aggregation_rule: report each strategy, regime and decision profile separately; no cross-profile composite or pooled robustness score

interpretation_guardrails: The lower/upper interval is an ambiguity set for a Bernoulli event probability, not a guarantee that the true probability is contained.
Worst-case expected-loss and minimax-regret policies are evaluated separately because they optimize different objectives.
Minimax regret compares each chosen action to the best action that would have been selected if the event probability were known.
Tie-breaking is frozen: choose no_action for exact worst-case minimax-regret ties.
The perfect-information oracle is an unattainable lower bound.
The point forecast policy remains the reference to show what the ambiguity set changes.
All weighted policy losses use the declared target/proposal stratum design; effective sample sizes accompany every policy/regime/profile result.
The ambiguity radii are synthetic protocol parameters, not inferred confidence levels and not tuned on a hidden test set.
No outcome-based action is attributed to the forecasting model after an abstention.
No composite resilience, political, loyalty, enlistment or personal-suitability score is accepted.
